package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService;
import android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityServiceInfo;
import android.content.ActivityNotFoundException;
import android.content.ComponentName;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.media.AudioManager;
import android.media.tv.TvContract;
import android.os.Build;
import android.provider.Settings;
import android.os.Handler;
import android.os.Looper;
import android.view.KeyEvent;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Consumer;
import java.util.function.ToIntFunction;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * Remote buttons that only the stock launcher answered, for InputKeyService and HomeKeyService: app_keys
 * (config.xml or a theme) maps a keycode to the app it opens, as "190:com.google.android.youtube.tv" or
 * "KEYCODE_BUTTON_3:com.google.android.youtube.tv", or a scancode as "scan:490:com.wbd.hbomax". A "hold:"
 * prefix makes an entry the long-press action instead: "hold:KEYCODE_BUTTON_8:org.xbmc.kodi" opens Kodi when
 * that button is held for HOLD_MS, while the unprefixed entry still opens on a tap; "hold:scan:490:..." does
 * the same for a scancode. One set of maps for both services; Android hands a key to every service that filters,
 * so both may call handle() for one event, and it answers each press once.
 * A target of "input:<input id>" switches to that TV input (an HDMI port) instead of opening an app, a target
 * of "inputs" opens the input switcher, for a remote whose source button sends a key Android does not map,
 * one of the action words (back, home, recents, mute, sleep, screensaver, settings, wifi, library) does that action, and
 * "package/.Activity" opens that activity rather than the app's launcher entry (an add-on's quick bar, say).
 */
final class RemoteKeys {

    /** How long a button is held before its "hold:" entry wins (Android's long-press timeout). */
    static final long HOLD_MS = 500;

    /** The app_keys target that opens the input switcher, as "scan:365:inputs". */
    static final String INPUTS = "inputs";

    /** Pre-compiled regex patterns to avoid re-compiling Patterns on every entry during key parsing. */
    private static final Pattern NUMERIC_KEY = Pattern.compile("[0-9]{1,6}");
    private static final Pattern KEYCODE_KEY = Pattern.compile("KEYCODE_[A-Z0-9_]+");

    private RemoteKeys() { }

    /** keycode -> package, with key names resolved by Android. */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseAppKeys(String[] entries) {
        return parseAppKeys(Arrays.asList(entries), KeyEvent::keyCodeFromString);
    }

    static Map<Integer, String> parseAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries) {
        return parseAppKeys(entries, KeyEvent::keyCodeFromString);
    }

    /**
     * keycode -> package. The key is a number or a KEYCODE_ name (resolved by {@code names}; 0, KEYCODE_UNKNOWN,
     * means it isn't one). Entries without a colon, with an unknown key or with no package are skipped; for a
     * keycode listed twice the last entry wins.
     */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries, ToIntFunction<String> names) {
        Map<Integer, String> keys = new HashMap<>();
        for (String entry : entries) {
            if (entry == null) continue;
            String[] parts = entry.split(":", 2);
            if (parts.length != 2 || parts[1].trim().isEmpty()) continue;
            String key = parts[0].trim();
            int code;
            if (NUMERIC_KEY.matcher(key).matches()) {
                code = Integer.parseInt(key);
            } else if (KEYCODE_KEY.matcher(key).matches()) {
                code = names.applyAsInt(key);   // keyCodeFromString takes digits only from API 29, names always
            } else {
                continue;
            }
            if (code > 0) keys.put(code, parts[1].trim());
        }
        return keys;
    }

    /** keycode -> package from the "hold:" entries; the rest of each entry reads as it does in parseAppKeys. */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseHoldAppKeys(String[] entries) {
        return parseHoldAppKeys(Arrays.asList(entries), KeyEvent::keyCodeFromString);
    }

    static Map<Integer, String> parseHoldAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries) {
        return parseHoldAppKeys(entries, KeyEvent::keyCodeFromString);
    }

    static Map<Integer, String> parseHoldAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries, ToIntFunction<String> names) {
        return parseAppKeys(prefixed(entries, "hold:"), names);
    }

    /** keycode -> target from the "front:" entries, used while the button's own app is already in front. */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseFrontAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries) {
        return parseFrontAppKeys(entries, KeyEvent::keyCodeFromString);
    }

    static Map<Integer, String> parseFrontAppKeys(Iterable<String> entries, ToIntFunction<String> names) {
        return parseAppKeys(prefixed(entries, "front:"), names);
    }

    static Map<Integer, String> parseFrontAppScancodes(Iterable<String> entries) {
        return parseAppScancodes(prefixed(entries, "front:"));
    }

    /**
     * Applies the key_filter choice (config.xml or a theme): when false the service drops
     * FLAG_REQUEST_FILTER_KEY_EVENTS at runtime, so it stays enabled for nothing but stops filtering.
     * Some firmware (TCL Google TV on Android 12) drops key auto-repeat once ANY service filters keys:
     * long-pressing volume then steps once per press. Filtering can only be skipped while the service
     * runs, since the flag is also declared in the manifest metadata.
     */
    static void applyKeyFilter(AccessibilityService service, boolean keyFilter) {
        if (keyFilter) return;
        AccessibilityServiceInfo info = service.getServiceInfo();
        if (info == null) return;
        info.flags &= ~AccessibilityServiceInfo.FLAG_REQUEST_FILTER_KEY_EVENTS;
        service.setServiceInfo(info);
    }

    /**
     * scancode -> package, from the "scan:490:com.wbd.hbomax" entries of the same list. For remotes that send
     * several app buttons as one keycode and tell them apart by scancode (Sony BRAVIA: YouTube, Prime Video and
     * Disney+ are all keycode 196, scancodes 485, 490 and 491). Find it with `getevent -t` while pressing the
     * button: the EV_KEY code, the hex number after 0001 on its line, which this list takes in decimal (01ea is 490).
     * Other entries are skipped; for a scancode listed twice the last entry wins.
     */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseAppScancodes(Iterable<String> entries) {
        Map<Integer, String> keys = new HashMap<>();
        for (String entry : entries) {
            if (entry == null) continue;
            String[] parts = entry.split(":", 3);
            if (parts.length != 3 || !parts[0].trim().equals("scan") || parts[2].trim().isEmpty()) continue;
            String code = parts[1].trim();
            if (!NUMERIC_KEY.matcher(code).matches()) continue;
            int scan = Integer.parseInt(code);
            if (scan > 0) keys.put(scan, parts[2].trim());
        }
        return keys;
    }

    /** scancode -> package from the "hold:scan:..." entries; the rest reads as it does in parseAppScancodes. */
    static Map<Integer, String> parseHoldAppScancodes(Iterable<String> entries) {
        return parseAppScancodes(prefixed(entries, "hold:"));
    }

    /** The entries with this prefix ("hold:", "front:"), the prefix removed, so the normal parsers can read them. */
    private static Iterable<String> prefixed(Iterable<String> entries, String prefix) {
        List<String> found = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String entry : entries) {
            if (entry == null) continue;
            String text = entry.trim();
            if (text.startsWith(prefix)) found.add(text.substring(prefix.length()).trim());
        }
        return found;
    }

    /** The package of a "guide:<package>" target, or null for any other target. */
    static String guidePackage(String target) {
        if (target == null || !target.startsWith("guide:")) return null;
        String pkg = target.substring(6).trim();
        return pkg.isEmpty() ? null : pkg;
    }

    /**
     * True when a tap's target is the app already in front ("package" or "package/.Activity"), so its "front:"
     * entry applies instead. Inputs and action words never match.
     */
    static boolean inFront(String target, String front) {
        if (target == null || front == null || front.isEmpty()) return false;
        int slash = target.indexOf('/');
        return (slash < 0 ? target : target.substring(0, slash)).equals(front);
    }

    /** The app in front, from HomeKeyService's window changes while app_keys has "front:" entries; "" otherwise. */
    static String frontPackage = "";

    /** A tap's target for both helpers: its "front:" entry while the button's own app is in front, else the usual one. */
    static String tap(String target, String alt) {
        return alt != null && inFront(target, frontPackage) ? alt : target;
    }

    /** Created on first use: building a Handler while the class loads breaks the JVM tests. */
    private static Presses presses;

    /**
     * Consumes a key mapped by either list: the hold app opens once the button has been down for HOLD_MS, the
     * normal one on an earlier release. False means neither list has this key, so the caller can pass it on.
     */
    static boolean handle(Context ctx, KeyEvent event, String app, String holdApp) {
        if (app == null && holdApp == null) return false;
        if (presses == null) {
            Handler handler = new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper());
            presses = new Presses(new Presses.Timer() {
                @Override public void post(Runnable hold, long delayMs) { handler.postDelayed(hold, delayMs); }
                @Override public void cancel(Runnable hold) { handler.removeCallbacks(hold); }
            });
        }
        String button = event.getDeviceId() + ":" + event.getKeyCode() + ":" + event.getScanCode();
        if (event.getAction() == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN) {
            presses.down(button, event.getEventTime(), event.getRepeatCount(), holdApp, ctx,
                    target -> launch(ctx, target));
        } else if (event.getAction() == KeyEvent.ACTION_UP) {
            presses.up(button, event.getEventTime(), event.getDownTime(), event.isCanceled(), app, holdApp,
                    target -> launch(ctx, target));
        }
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * For a helper that stops receiving keys (unbound, destroyed, or no longer filtering): no UP will reach it to
     * cancel a hold it saw go down, so the hold goes to the other helper if that one saw the DOWN too, and is
     * cancelled otherwise. Safe to call more than once.
     */
    static void release(Context helper) {
        if (presses != null) presses.release(helper);
    }

    /**
     * Each button's presses, kept per device, keycode and scancode: KeyEvent.getDownTime() can't tell presses apart,
     * since a key pressed together with another can report the other's. Both services get every event, so a DOWN
     * or UP whose event time was already seen for that button is the other service's copy and is skipped. One small
     * record per mapped button that has been pressed, not a history.
     */
    static final class Presses {
        interface Timer {
            void post(Runnable hold, long delayMs);
            void cancel(Runnable hold);
        }

        private static final class Press {
            long downAt = -1, upAt = -1;
            boolean fired;
            Runnable hold;
            /** The helpers that saw this DOWN while its hold is pending, each with the way it opens a target. */
            final Map<Object, Consumer<String>> owners = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        }

        private final Map<String, Press> buttons = new HashMap<>();
        private final Timer timer;

        Presses(Timer timer) {
            this.timer = timer;
        }

        void down(String button, long eventTime, int repeatCount, String holdApp, Object owner,
                Consumer<String> open) {
            if (repeatCount != 0) return;
            Press press = buttons.computeIfAbsent(button, b -> new Press());
            if (press.downAt == eventTime) {
                // The other helper's copy: it can answer the hold too, should the first one leave.
                if (press.hold != null) press.owners.putIfAbsent(owner, open);
                return;
            }
            if (press.hold != null) timer.cancel(press.hold);   // its UP never came
            press.downAt = eventTime;
            press.fired = false;
            press.hold = null;
            press.owners.clear();
            if (holdApp == null) return;
            press.owners.put(owner, open);
            press.hold = () -> {
                Consumer<String> first = press.owners.values().iterator().next();
                press.hold = null;
                press.owners.clear();
                press.fired = true;
                first.accept(holdApp);
            };
            timer.post(press.hold, HOLD_MS);
        }

        /** Drops this helper from every pending hold, cancelling a hold it was the last to own. */
        void release(Object owner) {
            for (Press press : buttons.values()) {
                if (press.hold == null || press.owners.remove(owner) == null || !press.owners.isEmpty()) continue;
                timer.cancel(press.hold);
                press.hold = null;
                press.fired = true;   // the press is over: an UP that still comes later opens nothing
            }
        }

        void up(String button, long eventTime, long downTime, boolean canceled, String app, String holdApp,
                Consumer<String> open) {
            Press press = buttons.computeIfAbsent(button, b -> new Press());
            if (press.upAt == eventTime) return;
            boolean sawDown = press.downAt > press.upAt;
            press.upAt = eventTime;
            if (press.hold != null) {
                timer.cancel(press.hold);
                press.hold = null;
                press.owners.clear();
            }
            if (canceled || (sawDown && press.fired)) return;
            // Without its DOWN (the service started while the button was held), the event's own down time will do.
            open.accept(target(app, holdApp, eventTime - (sawDown ? press.downAt : downTime)));
        }
    }

    /**
     * The flags on the KEYCODE_MENU pair that Xiaomi's China firmware (MiTV-MFTR0, Android 11) injects for a short
     * press of the remote's Menu key, after keeping the real press for itself (#1637). They include FLAG_CANCELED,
     * so the pair reads as a cancelled press, and the undocumented 0x1000, 0x2000 and 0x4000, which no real
     * cancelled press carries.
     */
    static final int XIAOMI_SHORT_MENU_FLAGS = 0x7531;

    /** Channel Up or Down, for home_ignore_channel_keys. */
    static boolean isChannelKey(int keyCode) {
        return keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_CHANNEL_UP || keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_CHANNEL_DOWN;
    }

    /** True for the UP that ends a Menu press: not cancelled, or cancelled only as Xiaomi's injected short press is. */
    static boolean menuReleased(int action, int flags) {
        if (action != KeyEvent.ACTION_UP) return false;
        return (flags & KeyEvent.FLAG_CANCELED) == 0
                || (flags & XIAOMI_SHORT_MENU_FLAGS) == XIAOMI_SHORT_MENU_FLAGS;
    }

    /** The app a mapped key opens: its hold entry after HOLD_MS, otherwise its normal one. */
    static String target(String app, String holdApp, long heldMs) {
        return heldMs >= HOLD_MS && holdApp != null ? holdApp : app;
    }

    /** The TV input id of an "input:<id>" target, e.g. "input:com.tcl.tvinput/.passthroughinput.TvPassThroughService/HW1413743104"; null for a package. */
    static String inputId(String target) {
        if (target == null || !target.startsWith("input:")) return null;
        String id = target.substring("input:".length()).trim();
        return id.isEmpty() ? null : id;
    }

    /**
     * The accessibility global action for an action word, or 0 when the target is something else. "sleep" is
     * GLOBAL_ACTION_LOCK_SCREEN, which puts a TV in standby (as the Sleep Timer add-on does); Android has it from 28.
     */
    static int globalAction(String target, int sdk) {
        switch (target) {
            case "back": return AccessibilityService.GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK;
            case "home": return AccessibilityService.GLOBAL_ACTION_HOME;
            case "recents": return AccessibilityService.GLOBAL_ACTION_RECENTS;
            case "sleep": return sdk >= 28 ? AccessibilityService.GLOBAL_ACTION_LOCK_SCREEN : 0;
            default: return 0;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Whether a target is an action word rather than an app or an input. A package name always has a dot.
     * "ignore" does nothing on purpose: the button is swallowed, for a remote shortcut that is pressed by accident.
     */
    static boolean isAction(String target) {
        switch (target) {
            case "back": case "home": case "recents": case "mute": case "sleep":
            case "screensaver": case "settings": case "wifi": case "library": case "ignore":
                return true;
            default:
                return false;
        }
    }

    /** Runs an action word; false for an app or an input. Needs no permission the launcher does not already have. */
    private static boolean runAction(Context ctx, String target) {
        if (!isAction(target)) return false;
        int global = globalAction(target, Build.VERSION.SDK_INT);
        if (global != 0) {
            // Home's own fallback path (vendor keys only the focused window gets) has no global actions: a bound helper
            // performs them, so back, home, recents and sleep mapped to such a key are not swallowed.
            AccessibilityService service = ctx instanceof AccessibilityService ? (AccessibilityService) ctx
                    : HomeKeyService.running != null ? HomeKeyService.running : InputKeyService.running;
            if (service != null) service.performGlobalAction(global);
            return true;
        }
        switch (target) {
            case "mute":
                // The media stream a TV plays everything on, with its own volume bar, as a remote's mute button would.
                AudioManager audio = ctx.getSystemService(AudioManager.class);
                if (audio != null) audio.adjustStreamVolume(AudioManager.STREAM_MUSIC,
                        AudioManager.ADJUST_TOGGLE_MUTE, AudioManager.FLAG_SHOW_UI);
                break;
            case "screensaver":
                // The screensaver chosen in the TV's settings, through the system's "start now" shortcut; the
                // launcher's own clock where the firmware has no such shortcut.
                Intent dream = new Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN)
                        .setClassName("com.android.systemui", "com.android.systemui.Somnambulator");
                if (ctx.getPackageManager().resolveActivity(dream, 0) == null) dream = new Intent(ctx, ClockActivity.class);
                start(ctx, dream);
                break;
            case "settings":
                start(ctx, SystemSettings.intent(ctx, Settings.ACTION_SETTINGS));
                break;
            case "wifi":
                start(ctx, SystemSettings.intent(ctx, Settings.ACTION_WIFI_SETTINGS));
                break;
            case "library":
                // Home with the App library open on top; Home does nothing when app_library is off.
                start(ctx, new Intent(ctx, MainActivity.class).setAction(MainActivity.ACTION_APP_LIBRARY));
                break;
            default:
                break;   // "ignore", or "sleep" below Android 9: consumed, nothing to do
        }
        return true;
    }

    private static void start(Context ctx, Intent intent) {
        try {
            ctx.startActivity(intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK));
        } catch (ActivityNotFoundException | SecurityException ignored) {
        }
    }

    /**
     * True for a "package/.Activity" target. An input id has slashes too, and ComponentName.unflattenFromString()
     * would read "input:com.tcl.tvinput" as its package, so an "input:" target never counts.
     */
    static boolean isActivity(String target) {
        return target != null && inputId(target) == null && target.indexOf('/') > 0;
    }

    /** Opens an app from a remote button: its TV entry if it has one, else its phone entry. An "input:<id>" target
     *  switches to that TV input (an HDMI port) instead, an action word runs that action, and a
     *  "package/.Activity" target opens that activity. */
    static void launch(Context ctx, String pkg) {
        if (pkg == null || runAction(ctx, pkg)) return;
        if (INPUTS.equals(pkg)) {
            // This launcher's own Inputs menu, as InputsRequestActivity opens it: addressed to Home directly, so a
            // vendor input picker that also answers VIEW_INPUTS never turns it into a chooser.
            try {
                ctx.startActivity(new Intent(ctx, MainActivity.class).setAction(MainActivity.ACTION_VIEW_INPUTS)
                        .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK));
            } catch (ActivityNotFoundException ignored) {
            }
            return;
        }
        String guide = guidePackage(pkg);
        if (guide != null) {
            // The program guide, asked for the way Android TV's Live TV apps take it: the programs directory.
            start(ctx, new Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW)
                    .setDataAndType(TvContract.Programs.CONTENT_URI, "vnd.android.cursor.dir/program")
                    .setPackage(guide));
            return;
        }
        String inputId = inputId(pkg);
        if (inputId != null) {
            // The same passthrough URI the Inputs menu opens, which the Live TV app handles.
            Intent view = new Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW)
                    .setDataAndType(TvContract.buildChannelUriForPassthroughInput(inputId),
                            "vnd.android.cursor.item/channel")
                    .addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK);
            // Aimed at the Live TV app first, as the Inputs menu does: an app that also claims the channel URI
            // (the Fluffy file manager on a TCL G03) turned the press into a chooser.
            String liveTv = Config.load(ctx).liveTvPackage;
            if (liveTv != null && !liveTv.isEmpty()) {
                try {
                    ctx.startActivity(new Intent(view).setPackage(liveTv));
                    return;
                } catch (ActivityNotFoundException | SecurityException ignored) {
                }
            }
            try {
                ctx.startActivity(view);
            } catch (ActivityNotFoundException | SecurityException ignored) {
            }
            return;
        }
        ComponentName activity = isActivity(pkg) ? ComponentName.unflattenFromString(pkg) : null;
        if (activity != null) {
            try {
                ctx.startActivity(new Intent().setComponent(activity).addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK));
            } catch (ActivityNotFoundException | SecurityException ignored) {
            }
            return;
        }
        Intent open = ctx.getPackageManager().getLeanbackLaunchIntentForPackage(pkg);
        if (open == null) open = ctx.getPackageManager().getLaunchIntentForPackage(pkg);
        if (open == null) return;
        try {
            ctx.startActivity(open.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK));
        } catch (ActivityNotFoundException | SecurityException ignored) {
        }
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\ServiceRepair.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.Manifest;
import android.content.ComponentName;
import android.content.ContentResolver;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.SharedPreferences;
import android.content.pm.PackageManager;
import android.provider.Settings;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Android takes an app's accessibility services off the enabled list when the app is force-stopped (Settings, a
 * cleaner app, or am force-stop), and the remote's Home, Input and app buttons then stop working until the helper
 * is turned on again over ADB. With restore_key_services on, a running helper records itself here and drops the
 * record when Android unbinds it (the user turned it off); a force stop kills the process before that, so the
 * record stays. Home starting again puts recorded helpers back on the list, when the installer granted
 * WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS. With the flag off nothing is recorded and nothing is restored.
 */
final class ServiceRepair {
    private static final String PREFS = "accessibility_helpers";

    private ServiceRepair() {
    }

    static void connected(Context context, Class<?> service) {
        prefs(context).edit().putBoolean(service.getName(), true).apply();
    }

    static void disconnected(Context context, Class<?> service) {
        prefs(context).edit().remove(service.getName()).apply();
    }

    static void restore(Context context) {
        if (context.checkSelfPermission(Manifest.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS)
                != PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED) return;
        try {
            ContentResolver cr = context.getContentResolver();
            String list = Settings.Secure.getString(cr, Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES);
            List<ComponentName> enabled = new ArrayList<>();
            if (list != null) {
                for (String entry : list.split(":")) {
                    ComponentName name = ComponentName.unflattenFromString(entry);
                    if (name != null) enabled.add(name);
                }
            }
            List<ComponentName> recorded = new ArrayList<>();
            for (String service : prefs(context).getAll().keySet()) {
                recorded.add(new ComponentName(context.getPackageName(), service));
            }
            if (recorded.isEmpty()) return;
            // The list without our recorded helpers, then with all of them.
            StringBuilder others = new StringBuilder();
            for (ComponentName name : enabled) {
                if (recorded.contains(name)) continue;
                if (others.length() > 0) others.append(':');
                others.append(name.flattenToShortString());
            }
            StringBuilder updated = new StringBuilder(others);
            boolean missing = false;
            for (ComponentName name : recorded) {
                if (!enabled.contains(name)) missing = true;
                if (updated.length() > 0) updated.append(':');
                updated.append(name.flattenToShortString());
            }
            // Hisense songshan's standby kill leaves the list naming the helper and only drops the switch to 0, with
            // the helper marked crashed (#3404): a confirmed 0 needs the same cycle. Default -1, so an absent or
            // unreadable switch with a complete list is left alone.
            if (!missing && Settings.Secure.getInt(cr, Settings.Secure.ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED, -1) != 0) return;
            // A killed helper also lands on Android's "Crashed services" list (dumpsys accessibility), and a
            // crashed service is never bound again, so putting it back on the list alone binds nothing and the
            // switch falls back to 0 (Hisense songshan, Android 11, whose standby kills third-party apps). Android
            // drops the crashed mark when it sees the helper leave the enabled list, so add, remove, add: after a
            // force stop the list is already empty, and a removal that changes nothing is not seen. Off the main
            // thread, so Home does not wait for the pauses. Each write first checks the list still reads what the
            // previous step left, and the cycle stops otherwise: a service turned on or off during a pause stays
            // that way instead of being overwritten by a snapshot.
            final String without = others.toString();
            final String with = updated.toString();
            new Thread(() -> {
                try {
                    if (!replaceList(cr, list, with)) return;
                    Thread.sleep(1000);
                    if (!replaceList(cr, with, without)) return;
                    Thread.sleep(1000);
                    if (!replaceList(cr, without, with)) return;
                    Settings.Secure.putInt(cr, Settings.Secure.ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED, 1);
                } catch (RuntimeException | InterruptedException ignored) {
                    // The setting is the system's; a refusal leaves the helper off, as before.
                }
            }, "ServiceRepair").start();
        } catch (RuntimeException ignored) {
            // The setting is the system's; a refusal leaves the helper off, as before.
        }
    }

    /** Writes the enabled list only while it still reads {@code expected}; an absent list counts as empty. */
    private static boolean replaceList(ContentResolver cr, String expected, String updated) {
        String now = Settings.Secure.getString(cr, Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES);
        return Objects.equals(now == null ? "" : now, expected == null ? "" : expected)
                && Settings.Secure.putString(cr, Settings.Secure.ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES, updated);
    }

    private static SharedPreferences prefs(Context context) {
        return context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE);
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.res.Resources;

import java.util.Calendar;

/** Solar Hijri (Shamsi) date with localized month names, without ICU: the arithmetic is small and stable. */
final class Shamsi {

    private static final int[] MONTHS = {
            R.string.shamsi_month_farvardin, R.string.shamsi_month_ordibehesht, R.string.shamsi_month_khordad,
            R.string.shamsi_month_tir, R.string.shamsi_month_mordad, R.string.shamsi_month_shahrivar,
            R.string.shamsi_month_mehr, R.string.shamsi_month_aban, R.string.shamsi_month_azar,
            R.string.shamsi_month_dey, R.string.shamsi_month_bahman, R.string.shamsi_month_esfand};

    private Shamsi() {
    }

    /** e.g. "27 Mehr 1405" */
    static String today(Resources res) {
        Calendar c = Calendar.getInstance();
        int[] j = toJalali(c.get(Calendar.YEAR), c.get(Calendar.MONTH) + 1, c.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH));
        return j[2] + " " + res.getString(MONTHS[j[1] - 1]) + " " + j[0];
    }

    /** Gregorian to Jalali, the 33-year-cycle algorithm used by jalaali-js. Returns {year, month, day}. */
    static int[] toJalali(int gy, int gm, int gd) {
        int[] monthStart = {0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334};
        int gy2 = gm > 2 ? gy + 1 : gy;
        int days = 355666 + 365 * gy + (gy2 + 3) / 4 - (gy2 + 99) / 100 + (gy2 + 399) / 400 + gd + monthStart[gm - 1];
        int jy = -1595 + 33 * (days / 12053);
        days %= 12053;
        jy += 4 * (days / 1461);
        days %= 1461;
        if (days > 365) {
            jy += (days - 1) / 365;
            days = (days - 1) % 365;
        }
        int jm, jd;
        if (days < 186) {
            jm = 1 + days / 31;
            jd = 1 + days % 31;
        } else {
            jm = 7 + (days - 186) / 30;
            jd = 1 + (days - 186) % 30;
        }
        return new int[]{jy, jm, jd};
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

/**
 * Time-of-day sky palette for the optional "sunset" backdrop (config.xml, sky_intensity).
 *
 * Pure maths, no Android types and no clock of its own: the caller passes minutes since midnight,
 * so the palette can be tested on the JVM. The colours are interpolated between a handful of
 * anchor points through the day, which is what makes the backdrop drift from night to dawn to
 * sunset instead of switching at fixed hours. Every colour stays dark enough for the white
 * text, the hero name and the dock band to keep their contrast.
 */
final class Sky {

    /** One anchor: a minute of the day and the values the palette takes exactly there. */
    static final class Stop {
        final int minute;
        final int top;
        final int mid;
        final int bottom;
        /** Alpha of the sun/moon glow near the horizon, 0 to 255. */
        final int sun;
        /** Horizontal position of the glow, 0 = left edge, 1 = right edge. */
        final float sunX;

        Stop(int minute, int top, int mid, int bottom, int sun, float sunX) {
            this.minute = minute;
            this.top = top;
            this.mid = mid;
            this.bottom = bottom;
            this.sun = sun;
            this.sunX = sunX;
        }
    }

    /** The palette at one instant: the three gradient colours plus the glow. */
    static final class Palette {
        final int top;
        final int mid;
        final int bottom;
        final int sun;
        final float sunX;

        Palette(int top, int mid, int bottom, int sun, float sunX) {
            this.top = top;
            this.mid = mid;
            this.bottom = bottom;
            this.sun = sun;
            this.sunX = sunX;
        }
    }

    private static final int NIGHT_TOP = 0xFF04060E;
    private static final int NIGHT_MID = 0xFF070C1A;
    private static final int NIGHT_BOTTOM = 0xFF0B1326;

    // Anchors were picked around a temperate evening: full night until half past five, dawn before
    // seven, the warmest glow between seven in the evening and a quarter to eight. With a location
    // set, at(minute, sunrise, sunset) stretches this reference day onto the real one.
    static final int REF_SUNRISE = 450;
    static final int REF_SUNSET = 1140;
    private static final Stop[] STOPS = {
            new Stop(0, NIGHT_TOP, NIGHT_MID, NIGHT_BOTTOM, 0, 0.30f),
            new Stop(320, NIGHT_TOP, NIGHT_MID, NIGHT_BOTTOM, 0, 0.30f),
            new Stop(390, 0xFF160F2E, 0xFF3B2352, 0xFF8A4A6B, 100, 0.24f),
            new Stop(450, 0xFF12203F, 0xFF5C3A63, 0xFFD3674F, 160, 0.30f),
            new Stop(570, 0xFF0E1A33, 0xFF1F3557, 0xFF43648B, 90, 0.38f),
            new Stop(780, 0xFF0B1524, 0xFF17304F, 0xFF31587F, 60, 0.50f),
            new Stop(1020, 0xFF0D1526, 0xFF20395C, 0xFF4C5470, 90, 0.62f),
            new Stop(1140, 0xFF1B1030, 0xFF6C2E52, 0xFFE2704A, 190, 0.76f),
            new Stop(1185, 0xFF140C27, 0xFF4A2049, 0xFFA54A5C, 130, 0.82f),
            new Stop(1260, 0xFF0A0A1C, 0xFF191230, 0xFF3A1F49, 60, 0.86f),
            new Stop(1350, NIGHT_TOP, NIGHT_MID, NIGHT_BOTTOM, 0, 0.30f),
            new Stop(1440, NIGHT_TOP, NIGHT_MID, NIGHT_BOTTOM, 0, 0.30f),
    };

    private Sky() {
    }

    /**
     * The palette at {@code minuteOfDay} on a day whose sun rises at {@code sunrise} and sets at
     * {@code sunset} (minutes of the day): night, day and evening are each stretched piecewise so
     * the reference sunrise and sunset glows land on the real ones.
     */
    static Palette at(int minuteOfDay, int sunrise, int sunset) {
        if (sunrise <= 0 || sunset >= 1440 || sunrise >= sunset) return at(minuteOfDay);
        int m = Math.max(0, Math.min(1440, minuteOfDay));
        float ref;
        if (m < sunrise) ref = m * REF_SUNRISE / (float) sunrise;
        else if (m < sunset) ref = REF_SUNRISE + (m - sunrise) * (REF_SUNSET - REF_SUNRISE) / (float) (sunset - sunrise);
        else ref = REF_SUNSET + (m - sunset) * (1440 - REF_SUNSET) / (float) (1440 - sunset);
        return at(Math.round(ref));
    }

    /** The palette at {@code minuteOfDay}, clamped to a day. */
    static Palette at(int minuteOfDay) {
        int m = Math.max(0, Math.min(1440, minuteOfDay));
        Stop a = STOPS[0];
        Stop b = STOPS[STOPS.length - 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < STOPS.length - 1; i++) {
            if (m >= STOPS[i].minute && m <= STOPS[i + 1].minute) {
                a = STOPS[i];
                b = STOPS[i + 1];
                break;
            }
        }
        float t = b.minute == a.minute ? 0f : (m - a.minute) / (float) (b.minute - a.minute);
        return new Palette(
                lerpColor(a.top, b.top, t),
                lerpColor(a.mid, b.mid, t),
                lerpColor(a.bottom, b.bottom, t),
                lerp(a.sun, b.sun, t),
                lerp(a.sunX, b.sunX, t));
    }

    /** Minute of day, 0 to 1439, of a wall clock time. */
    static int minuteOfDay(int hour, int minute) {
        return Math.max(0, Math.min(23, hour)) * 60 + Math.max(0, Math.min(59, minute));
    }

    /** Blends two opaque ARGB colours channel by channel; {@code t} is 0 to 1. */
    static int lerpColor(int from, int to, float t) {
        float f = Math.max(0f, Math.min(1f, t));
        int a = Math.round(((from >>> 24) & 0xFF) + (((to >>> 24) & 0xFF) - ((from >>> 24) & 0xFF)) * f);
        int r = Math.round(((from >> 16) & 0xFF) + (((to >> 16) & 0xFF) - ((from >> 16) & 0xFF)) * f);
        int g = Math.round(((from >> 8) & 0xFF) + (((to >> 8) & 0xFF) - ((from >> 8) & 0xFF)) * f);
        int b = Math.round((from & 0xFF) + ((to & 0xFF) - (from & 0xFF)) * f);
        return (a << 24) | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
    }

    private static int lerp(int from, int to, float t) {
        return Math.round(from + (to - from) * Math.max(0f, Math.min(1f, t)));
    }

    private static float lerp(float from, float to, float t) {
        return from + (to - from) * Math.max(0f, Math.min(1f, t));
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.Context;
import android.graphics.Bitmap;
import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.LinearGradient;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.RadialGradient;
import android.graphics.Shader;
import android.graphics.drawable.BitmapDrawable;
import android.util.AttributeSet;
import android.view.Gravity;
import android.view.View;

import androidx.annotation.Nullable;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.util.Calendar;

/**
 * A full-screen gradient that follows the clock: night blues, a warm horizon at sunset, a soft
 * glow that travels with the sun. Off by default (config.xml, sky_intensity = 0); a theme turns
 * it on with {@code "sky_intensity": 60}.
 *
 * Like the ambient glow, the backdrop is one small bitmap (480x270) stretched over the screen:
 * a gradient repainted at full resolution every minute is exactly the CPU cost the ambient glow
 * was rewritten to avoid on weak GPUs. It is redrawn once a minute and never animated, so the
 * cost is a single full-screen draw per minute.
 */
public class SkyView extends View {

    /** Full-screen and faded with setAlpha: without this every redraw of Home goes through an offscreen layer. */
    @Override
    public boolean hasOverlappingRendering() {
        return false;
    }

    private static final int TEX_W = 480;
    private static final int TEX_H = 270;

    /** Opacity of the whole backdrop, 0 to 255, from sky_intensity. */
    private int intensity;
    private int lastMinute = -1;
    private Bitmap texture;
    private BitmapDrawable drawable;

    public SkyView(Context context, @Nullable AttributeSet attrs) {
        super(context, attrs);
    }

    /** {@code percent} of sky_intensity: 0 hides the backdrop, 100 covers the wallpaper. */
    public void setIntensity(int percent) {
        intensity = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, percent));
        setAlpha(intensity / 100f);
        setVisibility(intensity == 0 ? GONE : VISIBLE);
        if (intensity > 0) render(true);
    }

    /** Picks up a new time of day; cheap and safe to call every minute. */
    public void update() {
        if (intensity == 0 || getVisibility() != VISIBLE) return;
        render(false);
    }

    @Override
    protected void onAttachedToWindow() {
        super.onAttachedToWindow();
        if (intensity > 0) render(true);
    }

    /** Today's sunrise and sunset at the configured place, or null without one (fixed reference day). */
    @Nullable
    private int[] sunTimes() {
        String lat = getContext().getString(R.string.latitude);
        String lon = getContext().getString(R.string.longitude);
        if (lat.isEmpty() || lon.isEmpty()) return null;
        try {
            return Sun.riseAndSet(LocalDate.now(), Double.parseDouble(lat), Double.parseDouble(lon),
                    ZoneId.systemDefault());
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private void render(boolean force) {
        Calendar now = Calendar.getInstance();
        int minute = Sky.minuteOfDay(now.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY), now.get(Calendar.MINUTE));
        if (!force && minute == lastMinute) return;
        lastMinute = minute;

        int[] sun = sunTimes();
        Sky.Palette sky = sun == null ? Sky.at(minute) : Sky.at(minute, sun[0], sun[1]);
        if (texture == null) texture = Bitmap.createBitmap(TEX_W, TEX_H, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888);
        Canvas canvas = new Canvas(texture);
        canvas.drawColor(0, android.graphics.PorterDuff.Mode.CLEAR);

        Paint paint = new Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG);
        paint.setShader(new LinearGradient(0f, 0f, 0f, TEX_H,
                new int[]{sky.top, sky.mid, sky.bottom},
                new float[]{0f, 0.55f, 1f}, Shader.TileMode.CLAMP));
        canvas.drawRect(0f, 0f, TEX_W, TEX_H, paint);

        if (sky.sun > 0) {
            // A warm core low on the horizon, where the sun (or its afterglow) sits.
            int warm = Sky.lerpColor(sky.bottom, 0xFFFFD9A0, 0.65f);
            paint.setShader(new RadialGradient(
                    sky.sunX * TEX_W, TEX_H * 0.80f, TEX_W * 0.55f,
                    new int[]{(sky.sun << 24) | (warm & 0x00FFFFFF), warm & 0x00FFFFFF},
                    new float[]{0f, 1f}, Shader.TileMode.CLAMP));
            canvas.drawRect(0f, 0f, TEX_W, TEX_H, paint);
        }

        if (drawable == null) {
            drawable = new BitmapDrawable(getResources(), texture);
            drawable.setGravity(Gravity.FILL);
            setBackground(drawable);
        }
        invalidate();
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.animation.Animator;
import android.animation.AnimatorListenerAdapter;
import android.animation.ValueAnimator;
import android.content.res.Resources;
import android.graphics.Bitmap;
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory;
import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.ColorFilter;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.PixelFormat;
import android.graphics.Rect;
import android.graphics.drawable.Drawable;
import android.view.animation.LinearInterpolator;

import androidx.annotation.NonNull;
import androidx.annotation.Nullable;

/**
 * A Halloween pill icon from a picture (Microsoft's Fluent Emoji 3D, MIT): a bat for Inputs that flaps its wings
 * twice when focused, or a ghost for Settings that drifts up and settles. The motion is a short scale or
 * offset of the same picture, played once per {@link #nudge()}; reduced motion leaves it still.
 */
public final class SpookyIconDrawable extends Drawable {

    static final int BAT = 0, GHOST = 1;

    private static final float BOX_DP = 24f;
    private static final long BAT_MS = 520, GHOST_MS = 900;

    private final int kind;
    private final float density;
    private final Bitmap bitmap;
    private final Paint paint = new Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG | Paint.FILTER_BITMAP_FLAG);
    private final Rect dst = new Rect();
    private final ValueAnimator animator;
    private float t = -1f;
    private boolean reduced;
    private int alpha = 255;

    public SpookyIconDrawable(Resources res, float density, int kind) {
        this.kind = kind;
        this.density = density;
        bitmap = BitmapFactory.decodeResource(res,
                kind == BAT ? R.drawable.halloween_bat : R.drawable.halloween_ghost);
        animator = ValueAnimator.ofFloat(0f, 1f);
        animator.setDuration(kind == BAT ? BAT_MS : GHOST_MS);
        animator.setInterpolator(new LinearInterpolator());
        animator.addUpdateListener(a -> {
            t = (float) a.getAnimatedValue();
            invalidateSelf();
        });
        animator.addListener(new AnimatorListenerAdapter() {
            @Override
            public void onAnimationEnd(Animator a) {
                t = -1f;
                invalidateSelf();
            }
        });
    }

    /** The focus motion: two wing beats for the bat, a float up and back for the ghost. */
    public void nudge() {
        if (reduced) return;
        animator.cancel();
        animator.start();
    }

    /** With reduced motion {@link #nudge()} does nothing and a motion in progress stops at rest. */
    public void setReducedMotion(boolean reducedMotion) {
        reduced = reducedMotion;
        if (reduced && animator.isRunning()) animator.cancel();
    }

    @Override
    public void draw(@NonNull Canvas canvas) {
        Rect b = getBounds();
        float sx = 1f, sy = 1f, dy = 0f, rot = 0f;
        if (t >= 0f) {
            if (kind == BAT) {
                // two beats: the wings fold (the picture squeezes vertically) and open again
                float beat = (float) Math.sin(t * 2 * Math.PI * 2);
                sy = 1f - 0.28f * Math.abs(beat);
                sx = 1f + 0.06f * Math.abs(beat);
                dy = -1.5f * density * (float) Math.sin(t * Math.PI);
            } else {
                // drifts up about 3 dp, tilting slightly, then sinks back
                float up = (float) Math.sin(t * Math.PI);
                dy = -3f * density * up;
                rot = 6f * (float) Math.sin(t * 2 * Math.PI) * (1f - t);
            }
        }
        int save = canvas.save();
        canvas.translate(b.exactCenterX(), b.exactCenterY() + dy);
        canvas.rotate(rot);
        canvas.scale(sx, sy);
        int hw = b.width() / 2, hh = b.height() / 2;
        dst.set(-hw, -hh, b.width() - hw, b.height() - hh);
        paint.setAlpha(alpha);
        canvas.drawBitmap(bitmap, null, dst, paint);
        canvas.restoreToCount(save);
    }

    @Override
    public int getIntrinsicWidth() {
        return Math.round(BOX_DP * density);
    }

    @Override
    public int getIntrinsicHeight() {
        return Math.round(BOX_DP * density);
    }

    @Override
    public void setAlpha(int alpha) {
        if (this.alpha == alpha) return;
        this.alpha = alpha;
        invalidateSelf();
    }

    @Override
    public int getAlpha() {
        return alpha;
    }

    @Override
    public void setColorFilter(@Nullable ColorFilter filter) {
        paint.setColorFilter(filter);
        invalidateSelf();
    }

    @Override
    @SuppressWarnings("deprecation")
    public int getOpacity() {
        return PixelFormat.TRANSLUCENT;
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** Isolate complete measurements, not individual digits, in the Hebrew stats paragraph. */
final class StatsText {
    private static final Pattern MEASUREMENT = Pattern.compile("[0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?(?:\\s*/\\s*[0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?)?(?:\\s+(?:MB|GB)|%)");
    static String forLocale(String text, Locale locale) {
        String language = locale.getLanguage();
        if (!language.equals("he") && !language.equals("iw")) return text;
        Matcher matcher = MEASUREMENT.matcher(text);
        StringBuffer isolated = new StringBuffer();
        while (matcher.find()) matcher.appendReplacement(isolated, Matcher.quoteReplacement("\u200E\u202A" + matcher.group() + "\u202C\u200E"));
        matcher.appendTail(isolated);
        // Embeddings plus directional marks also work on TV text renderers that mishandle isolates.
        return "\u200F" + isolated.toString().replace("  ·  ", "\u200F  ·  \u200F");
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.ZoneId;

/**
 * Sunrise and sunset for a place, computed offline with NOAA's general solar position equations
 * (accurate to a few minutes, which is plenty for a backdrop). Pure maths, no Android types, so
 * it runs in JVM tests; no network and no location permission, the place comes from config.xml.
 */
final class Sun {

    private Sun() {
    }

    /**
     * Local minutes of the day of sunrise and sunset, as {@code {sunrise, sunset}}, or null when the
     * sun does not rise or does not set that day (polar night or midnight sun).
     */
    static int[] riseAndSet(LocalDate date, double latitude, double longitude, ZoneId zone) {
        double g = 2 * Math.PI / 365 * (date.getDayOfYear() - 1);
        double eqTime = 229.18 * (0.000075 + 0.001868 * Math.cos(g) - 0.032077 * Math.sin(g)
                - 0.014615 * Math.cos(2 * g) - 0.040849 * Math.sin(2 * g));
        double decl = 0.006918 - 0.399912 * Math.cos(g) + 0.070257 * Math.sin(g)
                - 0.006758 * Math.cos(2 * g) + 0.000907 * Math.sin(2 * g)
                - 0.002697 * Math.cos(3 * g) + 0.00148 * Math.sin(3 * g);
        double lat = Math.toRadians(latitude);
        // 90.833 degrees: the sun's upper edge on the horizon, with refraction.
        double cosHa = Math.cos(Math.toRadians(90.833)) / (Math.cos(lat) * Math.cos(decl))
                - Math.tan(lat) * Math.tan(decl);
        if (cosHa > 1 || cosHa < -1) return null;
        double ha = Math.toDegrees(Math.acos(cosHa));
        int offset = zone.getRules().getOffset(date.atTime(12, 0)).getTotalSeconds() / 60;
        return new int[]{
                (int) Math.round(720 - 4 * (longitude + ha) - eqTime + offset),
                (int) Math.round(720 - 4 * (longitude - ha) - eqTime + offset)};
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.ComponentName;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.content.pm.PackageManager;
import android.content.pm.ResolveInfo;
import android.net.Uri;
import android.provider.Settings;

/** The standard settings intent, or, when nothing usable answers it, the first vendor settings entry
 *  from settings_fallback_components that is installed (Xiaomi China, TCL / FFALCON, Fire OS), else the
 *  AOSP TV settings app's main screen where it is installed. */
final class SystemSettings {
    private SystemSettings() {}

    static Intent intent(Context context, String action) {
        PackageManager pm = context.getPackageManager();
        Intent standard = new Intent(action);
        ResolveInfo resolved = pm.resolveActivity(standard, PackageManager.MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY);
        // Fire OS resolves the standard actions to a CTS compliance stub that opens nothing;
        // treat it as missing so the vendor fallback runs.
        if (resolved != null && !resolved.activityInfo.name.contains("CTSDummy")) return standard;
        Intent vendor = vendorIntent(context);
        if (vendor != null) return vendor;
        // Some firmware ships the AOSP TV settings app with no filter for the standard actions (HY300 Pro+
        // projector, rk3566, Android 14): open its main screen directly. Not a vendor entry, so the Settings
        // menu's "Native settings" row stays as it was.
        Intent aosp = new Intent().setComponent(AOSP_TV_SETTINGS);
        try {
            pm.getPackageInfo(AOSP_TV_SETTINGS.getPackageName(), 0);
            return aosp;
        } catch (PackageManager.NameNotFoundException e) {
            return standard;
        }
    }

    private static final ComponentName AOSP_TV_SETTINGS =
            new ComponentName("com.android.tv.settings", "com.android.tv.settings.MainSettings");

    /** The first vendor settings entry from settings_fallback_components that is installed, or null
     *  when none is. China-market firmware keeps pages the AOSP TV settings has no row for -
     *  Xiaomi's Account & Security, where the ADB switch lives - in the vendor's own settings app;
     *  MainActivity's Settings menu offers it as "Native settings" while one is installed. */
    static Intent vendorIntent(Context context) {
        PackageManager pm = context.getPackageManager();
        for (String value : context.getResources().getStringArray(R.array.settings_fallback_components)) {
            ComponentName component = ComponentName.unflattenFromString(value);
            if (component == null) continue;
            // Explicit resolveActivity() always succeeds, so check the package exists instead.
            try {
                pm.getPackageInfo(component.getPackageName(), 0);
            } catch (PackageManager.NameNotFoundException e) {
                continue;
            }
            return new Intent().setComponent(component);
        }
        return null;
    }

    /** The TV's App info page for pkg, or null where the firmware has none (CVTE's settings app, #1202). */
    static Intent appInfo(Context context, String pkg) {
        Intent info = new Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS, Uri.parse("package:" + pkg));
        return context.getPackageManager().resolveActivity(info, PackageManager.MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY) != null ? info : null;
    }

    /**
     * The TV's display or picture settings. On Xiaomi sets, the AOSP DISPLAY_SETTINGS action resolves to
     * an empty stub in DroidTvSettings; prefer Xiaomi's own PictureActivity where installed.
     */
    static Intent displayIntent(Context context) {
        ComponentName xiaomi = new ComponentName("com.android.tv.settings",
                "com.xiaomi.mitv.settings.picture.PictureActivity");
        if (context.getPackageManager().resolveActivity(new Intent().setComponent(xiaomi), 0) != null) {
            return new Intent().setComponent(xiaomi);
        }
        return intent(context, Settings.ACTION_DISPLAY_SETTINGS);
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** The files ThemeProvider may write or delete under Config.dir, by the URI's path segments. */
final class ThemeFiles {
    static final String WALLPAPERS = "wallpapers";
    /** The names tools/theme.sh accepts for a collection image, and the types WallpaperRotation reads. */
    private static final Pattern IMAGE = Pattern.compile("[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\\.(jpg|jpeg|png|webp)",
            Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE);

    private ThemeFiles() {}

    /** The path relative to the theme directory, e.g. "config.json" or "wallpapers/dusk.jpg", or null if refused. */
    static String path(List<String> segments) {
        if (segments == null) return null;
        if (segments.size() == 1) {
            String name = segments.get(0);
            return Config.FILE_NAME.equals(name) || "wallpaper.jpg".equals(name) || "theme_revision".equals(name)
                    ? name : null;
        }
        if (segments.size() == 2 && WALLPAPERS.equals(segments.get(0))
                && (collectionImage(segments.get(1)) || WallpaperCaptions.FILE_NAME.equals(segments.get(1)))) {
            return WALLPAPERS + "/" + segments.get(1);
        }
        return null;
    }

    /** True for "wallpapers" alone: a delete of it clears the collection's images. */
    static boolean isCollection(List<String> segments) {
        return segments != null && segments.size() == 1 && WALLPAPERS.equals(segments.get(0));
    }

    static boolean collectionImage(String name) {
        return name != null && !name.startsWith(".") && IMAGE.matcher(name).matches();
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.ContentProvider;
import android.content.ContentValues;
import android.database.Cursor;
import android.net.Uri;
import android.os.ParcelFileDescriptor;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.FileNotFoundException;

/**
 * Lets tools/theme.sh write the theme files into {@link Config#dir} on firmware where the adb shell is
 * locked out of Android/data (TCL G07, Android 11). Only the files {@link ThemeFiles} allows, and only for
 * callers holding WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, which the adb shell has and ordinary apps cannot get.
 *
 *   content write --uri content://com.gathin.tvhome.theme/config.json < /data/local/tmp/config.json
 *   content write --uri content://com.gathin.tvhome.theme/wallpapers/dusk.jpg < /data/local/tmp/dusk.jpg
 *   content delete --uri content://com.gathin.tvhome.theme/config.json
 *   content delete --uri content://com.gathin.tvhome.theme/wallpapers      (every image in the collection)
 */
public class ThemeProvider extends ContentProvider {

    private File file(Uri uri) throws FileNotFoundException {
        String path = ThemeFiles.path(uri.getPathSegments());
        File dir = Config.dir(getContext());
        if (dir == null || path == null) throw new FileNotFoundException(String.valueOf(uri));
        File f = new File(dir, path);
        File parent = f.getParentFile();
        if (parent != null && !parent.isDirectory() && !parent.mkdirs()) throw new FileNotFoundException(String.valueOf(uri));
        return f;
    }

    @Override
    public ParcelFileDescriptor openFile(Uri uri, String mode) throws FileNotFoundException {
        File f = file(uri);
        if (mode.contains("w")) {
            return ParcelFileDescriptor.open(f, ParcelFileDescriptor.MODE_WRITE_ONLY
                    | ParcelFileDescriptor.MODE_CREATE | ParcelFileDescriptor.MODE_TRUNCATE);
        }
        return ParcelFileDescriptor.open(f, ParcelFileDescriptor.MODE_READ_ONLY);
    }

    @Override
    public int delete(Uri uri, String selection, String[] selectionArgs) {
        File dir = Config.dir(getContext());
        if (dir != null && ThemeFiles.isCollection(uri.getPathSegments())) {
            File[] images = new File(dir, ThemeFiles.WALLPAPERS).listFiles((d, name) -> ThemeFiles.collectionImage(name));
            int n = 0;
            if (images != null) for (File f : images) if (f.delete()) n++;
            return n;
        }
        try {
            return file(uri).delete() ? 1 : 0;
        } catch (FileNotFoundException e) {
            return 0;
        }
    }

    @Override public boolean onCreate() { return true; }
    @Override public String getType(Uri uri) { return null; }
    @Override public Cursor query(Uri uri, String[] p, String s, String[] a, String o) { return null; }
    @Override public Uri insert(Uri uri, ContentValues values) { return null; }
    @Override public int update(Uri uri, ContentValues v, String s, String[] a) { return 0; }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\TileRefresh.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

/**
 * Whether Home rebuilds its tiles when it comes back to the front. A rebuild asks PackageManager for every app again
 * and reloads every banner, icon and label (about 30 ms on a TCL C755, on every Home press), so it happens only when
 * an app was installed, removed, updated, enabled or disabled in the meantime. Otherwise Home only puts the focus
 * back, as before.
 */
final class TileRefresh {

    enum Action { NOTHING, REFOCUS, REBUILD }

    private boolean started;
    /** The tiles may not match the installed apps: true until the first build. */
    private boolean stale = true;
    private boolean refocus;

    void onStart() {
        started = true;
    }

    /** Another app took the screen: its tiles stay, and focus goes back to them on the way in. */
    void onStop() {
        started = false;
        refocus = true;
    }

    /** Home pressed while Home is in front: back to the first tile. */
    void onHomeAgain() {
        refocus = true;
    }

    /** The tiles were dropped (onTrimMemory): build them again on the way back. */
    void invalidate() {
        stale = true;
    }

    /**
     * A package broadcast. True when Home is on screen and should rebuild now; while it is in the background the
     * rebuild waits for {@link #onResume}, so a run of app updates costs one rebuild instead of one each.
     */
    boolean onPackagesChanged() {
        if (started) return true;
        stale = true;
        return false;
    }

    /** @param changedMeanwhile PackageManager reports changed packages since the last build (a missed broadcast). */
    Action onResume(boolean changedMeanwhile) {
        Action action = stale || changedMeanwhile ? Action.REBUILD : refocus ? Action.REFOCUS : Action.NOTHING;
        stale = false;
        refocus = false;
        return action;
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\TopFade.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.LinearGradient;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.PorterDuff;
import android.graphics.PorterDuffXfermode;
import android.graphics.Shader;
import android.view.View;

import androidx.annotation.NonNull;
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView;

/**
 * fade_rows: the rows fade out as they scroll up under the clock, instead of being cut off at the grid's top
 * edge. It erases the top of the grid's own picture, so whatever is behind Home (a wallpaper, the sky) shows
 * through; the grid draws into a hardware layer for that ({@link #attach}), or the erasing would punch through
 * the whole window. Android's own requiresFadingEdge draws its fade in the wrong place with this grid's
 * clipChildren=false, so it is not used. The fade grows in over the first pixels of scrolling, so the dock at
 * rest is untouched.
 */
final class TopFade extends RecyclerView.ItemDecoration {

    private final float length;
    private final Paint paint = new Paint();
    private float shaderHeight = -1f;

    private TopFade(float length) {
        this.length = length;
        paint.setXfermode(new PorterDuffXfermode(PorterDuff.Mode.DST_OUT));
    }

    static void attach(RecyclerView grid, float length) {
        grid.setLayerType(View.LAYER_TYPE_HARDWARE, null);
        grid.addItemDecoration(new TopFade(length));
    }

    /** How tall the fade is after scrolling {@code scrolled} pixels: nothing at rest, then up to {@code length}. */
    static float height(int scrolled, float length) {
        return Math.max(0f, Math.min(length, scrolled));
    }

    @Override
    public void onDrawOver(@NonNull Canvas c, @NonNull RecyclerView parent, @NonNull RecyclerView.State state) {
        float fade = height(parent.computeVerticalScrollOffset(), length);
        if (fade <= 0f) return;
        if (fade != shaderHeight) {
            paint.setShader(new LinearGradient(0f, 0f, 0f, fade, 0xFF000000, 0x00000000, Shader.TileMode.CLAMP));
            shaderHeight = fade;
        }
        c.drawRect(0f, 0f, parent.getWidth(), fade, paint);
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.Context;

/**
 * The typeface behind one of the font_* strings in res/values/fonts.xml, for views built in code. The string
 * points at a bundled font, or, in locales Outfit can't draw (values-vi), names a system family (#833).
 */
final class UiFont {
    private UiFont() {}

    static Typeface get(Context context, int fontString) {
        Resources res = context.getResources();
        TypedValue value = new TypedValue();
        res.getValue(fontString, value, true);
        String name = String.valueOf(value.string);

`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\VolumeKeys.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.content.Context;
import android.media.AudioManager;
import android.os.Handler;
import android.os.Looper;
import android.view.KeyEvent;

/**
 * consume_volume_keys: some firmware (TCL G03, Android 11, #1100) applies a volume key before the key
 * services' filter and again when the service hands it back, so one tap moved two steps. The services swallow
 * Volume Up/Down instead, which leaves the firmware's first step; a swallowed key gets no auto-repeat, so a held
 * one is repeated here, from the same delay and at about the rate Android uses.
 *
 * The state is per process, not per service: with HomeKeyService and InputKeyService both bound, each sees the
 * same press, and the second call restarts the same repeat instead of adding a second one.
 */
final class VolumeKeys {
    static final long REPEAT_DELAY_MS = 500;
    static final long REPEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 60;

    /** Created on first use, so the class loads in JVM tests that only call the pure methods. */
    private static Handler handler;
    private static Runnable step;

    private VolumeKeys() {
    }

    /** AudioManager direction for a volume key, or 0 for any other key. */
    static int direction(int keyCode) {
        if (keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_VOLUME_UP) return AudioManager.ADJUST_RAISE;
        if (keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_VOLUME_DOWN) return AudioManager.ADJUST_LOWER;
        return 0;
    }

    /** Whether this event starts or ends a press; a repeated down event changes nothing. */
    static boolean changesPress(int action, int repeatCount) {
        return action != KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN || repeatCount == 0;
    }

    /** Swallows a volume key (true) and repeats it while held; any other key is left alone (false). */
    static boolean handle(Context context, KeyEvent event) {
        int direction = direction(event.getKeyCode());
        if (direction == 0) return false;
        if (!changesPress(event.getAction(), event.getRepeatCount())) return true;
        stop();
        if (event.getAction() != KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN) return true;
        AudioManager audio = context.getSystemService(AudioManager.class);
        if (audio == null) return true;
        if (handler == null) handler = new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper());
        step = new Runnable() {
            @Override
            public void run() {
                audio.adjustVolume(direction, AudioManager.FLAG_SHOW_UI);
                handler.postDelayed(this, REPEAT_INTERVAL_MS);
            }
        };
        handler.postDelayed(step, REPEAT_DELAY_MS);
        return true;
    }

    /** Ends a repeat in progress, e.g. when the service goes away while a key is held. */
    static void stop() {
        if (handler != null && step != null) handler.removeCallbacks(step);
        step = null;
    }
}

package com.gathin.tvhome;

import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.RectF;
import android.graphics.drawable.Drawable;
import android.graphics.drawable.GradientDrawable;
import android.graphics.drawable.StateListDrawable;
import android.text.style.ReplacementSpan;

import androidx.annotation.NonNull;

/**
 * The green "VPN" capsule drawn inside the network pill while a VPN is up: a lock and the word VPN, dark on
 * green, so it reads on both the frosted and the focused (white) pill. With a VPN app configured and no VPN
 * up, the same capsule turns red, without the lock, so a dropped VPN is noticed.
 */
final class VpnBadge extends ReplacementSpan {

    static final int GREEN = 0xFF30D158;
    static final int INK = 0xFF06290F;
    static final int RED = 0xFFFF453A;
    static final int INK_OFF = 0xFFFFFFFF;

    private final Drawable lock;
    private final float density;
    private final int fill, ink;
    private final RectF rect = new RectF();

    /** @param lock the lock icon for the "up" badge, or null for the red "off" badge */
    VpnBadge(Drawable lock, float density) {
        this.fill = lock != null ? GREEN : RED;
        this.ink = lock != null ? INK : INK_OFF;
        this.lock = lock != null ? lock.mutate() : null;
        if (this.lock != null) this.lock.setTint(ink);
        this.density = density;
    }

    /** vpn_pill: what the VPN pill shows, from {@link #pillState}. */
    static final int PILL_HIDDEN = 0, PILL_UP = 1, PILL_OFF = 2;

    /**
     * vpn_pill: green while any VPN is up, red "VPN off" while none is but the configured VPN app is installed (so a
     * dropped VPN is noticed), hidden while neither is true: no pill on a TV without a VPN.
     */
    static int pillState(boolean vpnUp, boolean vpnAppInstalled) {
        return vpnUp ? PILL_UP : vpnAppInstalled ? PILL_OFF : PILL_HIDDEN;
    }

    /** icon_only_vpn: the closed lock while a VPN is up, the open lock while none is. */
    static int iconOnlyLock(boolean up) {
        return up ? R.drawable.ic_lock : R.drawable.ic_lock_open;
    }

    /**
     * vpn_pill: the pill's background. At rest it is dark glass outlined in the state colour and only the focused state is
     * filled solid with a white ring — a solid pill at rest read as already selected, so OK pressed on a tile was
     * taken for a press on the pill.
     */
    static StateListDrawable pillBackground(boolean up, float density) {
        StateListDrawable bg = new StateListDrawable();
        GradientDrawable focused = pillShape(up, density);
        focused.setStroke(Math.round(3 * density), 0xFFFFFFFF);
        bg.addState(new int[]{android.R.attr.state_focused}, focused);
        // Dark glass, so the state colour reads over a bright wallpaper as well as a dark one.
        GradientDrawable rest = new GradientDrawable(GradientDrawable.Orientation.TOP_BOTTOM,
                new int[]{0xA6000000, 0x8C000000});
        rest.setCornerRadius(21 * density);
        rest.setStroke(Math.round(2 * density), up ? GREEN : RED);
        bg.addState(new int[0], rest);
        return bg;
    }

    /**
     * vpn_pill: the pill's text and icon colour. At rest the pill is an outline, so the ink is the state colour;
     * on the solid focused fill it is the contrasting ink.
     */
    static int pillInkColor(boolean up, boolean focused) {
        if (up) return focused ? INK : GREEN;
        return focused ? INK_OFF : RED;
    }

    private static GradientDrawable pillShape(boolean up, float density) {
        GradientDrawable shape = new GradientDrawable();
        shape.setColor(up ? GREEN : RED);
        shape.setCornerRadius(21 * density);
        return shape;
    }

    private float textSize(Paint p) {
        return p.getTextSize() * 0.78f;
    }

    private float lockSize(Paint p) {
        return lock != null ? p.getTextSize() * 0.8f : 0;
    }

    private float lockGap() {
        return lock != null ? 4 * density : 2 * density;
    }

    @Override
    public int getSize(@NonNull Paint paint, CharSequence text, int start, int end, Paint.FontMetricsInt fm) {
        float old = paint.getTextSize();
        paint.setTextSize(textSize(paint));
        float w = paint.measureText(text, start, end);
        paint.setTextSize(old);
        // margin + left pad + lock + gap + text + right pad
        return (int) (8 * density + 7 * density + lockSize(paint) + lockGap() + w + 9 * density);
    }

    @Override
    public void draw(@NonNull Canvas c, CharSequence text, int start, int end, float x, int top, int y, int bottom,
                     @NonNull Paint paint) {
        float base = paint.getTextSize();
        float lockPx = lockSize(paint);
        float h = base * 1.3f;
        float cy = (top + bottom) / 2f;
        float left = x + 8 * density;
        float right = x + getSize(paint, text, start, end, null);
        rect.set(left, cy - h / 2f, right, cy + h / 2f);

        int oldColor = paint.getColor();
        paint.setColor(fill);
        c.drawRoundRect(rect, h / 2f, h / 2f, paint);

        int lx = (int) (left + 7 * density);
        if (lock != null) {
            lock.setBounds(lx, (int) (cy - lockPx / 2f), (int) (lx + lockPx), (int) (cy + lockPx / 2f));
            lock.draw(c);
        }

        paint.setColor(ink);
        paint.setTextSize(textSize(paint));
        Paint.FontMetrics fm = paint.getFontMetrics();
        float ty = cy - (fm.ascent + fm.descent) / 2f;
        c.drawText(text, start, end, lx + lockPx + lockGap(), ty, paint);
        paint.setTextSize(base);
        paint.setColor(oldColor);
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\WallpaperCaptions.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.io.File;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Names for a wallpaper collection (wallpaper_captions): {@code wallpapers/captions.txt}, one
 * "filename<TAB>name" per line. Blank lines, lines starting with # and lines without a tab are skipped; a name
 * is cut to {@link #MAX_LENGTH} characters. No Android types, so it is tested on the JVM.
 */
final class WallpaperCaptions {
    static final String FILE_NAME = "captions.txt";
    static final int MAX_LENGTH = 80;

    private WallpaperCaptions() { }

    static Map<String, String> parse(List<String> lines) {
        Map<String, String> names = new HashMap<>();
        for (String line : lines) {
            if (line == null || line.trim().isEmpty() || line.trim().startsWith("#")) continue;
            int tab = line.indexOf('\t');
            if (tab <= 0) continue;
            String file = line.substring(0, tab).trim();
            String name = line.substring(tab + 1).trim();
            if (file.isEmpty() || name.isEmpty()) continue;
            if (name.length() > MAX_LENGTH) name = name.substring(0, MAX_LENGTH).trim();
            names.put(file, name);
        }
        return names;
    }

    /** The names in {@code folder}/captions.txt, or none when the file is missing or unreadable. */
    static Map<String, String> read(File folder) {
        File file = folder == null ? null : new File(folder, FILE_NAME);
        if (file == null || !file.isFile() || file.length() > 256 * 1024) return Collections.emptyMap();
        try {
            return parse(Files.readAllLines(file.toPath(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return Collections.emptyMap();
        }
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\WallpaperMood.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.io.File;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * wallpaper_moods: which group of a rotating wallpaper collection fits the time of day. Morning from sunrise to noon,
 * evening until half an hour after sunset, night the rest. The sun is the one at config.xml's latitude and longitude,
 * worked out offline by {@link Sun} as the sky does, or 07:00 and 18:30 without a place. A group that is missing, or
 * has none of the collection's pictures, falls back to the whole collection.
 */
final class WallpaperMood {
    static final String MORNING = "morning", EVENING = "evening", NIGHT = "night";
    static final String[] ALL = {MORNING, EVENING, NIGHT};
    /** Sunrise and sunset in minutes of the day, without a place (or where the sun does not rise or set that day). */
    static final int DEFAULT_SUNRISE = 7 * 60, DEFAULT_SUNSET = 18 * 60 + 30;
    private static final int NOON = 12 * 60;
    /** Evening lasts this long after sunset, while the sky still glows. */
    private static final int DUSK_MINUTES = 30;

    private WallpaperMood() {
    }

    /** The mood at this minute of the day, for a sunrise and sunset in minutes of the day. */
    static String timeOfDay(int minute, int sunrise, int sunset) {
        if (minute >= sunrise && minute < NOON) return MORNING;
        if (minute >= NOON && minute < sunset + DUSK_MINUTES) return EVENING;
        return NIGHT;
    }

    /** That day's {sunrise, sunset} at config.xml's latitude and longitude; the defaults when either is unusable. */
    static int[] sun(LocalDate day, String latitude, String longitude, ZoneId zone) {
        int[] times = null;
        try {
            if (!latitude.trim().isEmpty() && !longitude.trim().isEmpty()) {
                times = Sun.riseAndSet(day, Double.parseDouble(latitude.trim()), Double.parseDouble(longitude.trim()), zone);
            }
        } catch (NumberFormatException ignored) {
            // not a number: the defaults
        }
        return times != null ? times : new int[]{DEFAULT_SUNRISE, DEFAULT_SUNSET};
    }

    /** The pictures in the mood's group, in the collection's order; all of them when the group has none. */
    static List<File> select(List<File> all, Map<String, Set<String>> groups, String mood) {
        Set<String> names = groups.get(mood);
        if (names == null) return all;
        List<File> group = new ArrayList<>();
        for (File file : all) if (names.contains(file.getName())) group.add(file);
        return group.isEmpty() ? all : group;
    }
}
