    private final Random random = new Random();
    private final int width;
    /** config wallpaper_true_color: ARGB_8888 instead of RGB_565. */
    private final Bitmap.Config bitmapConfig;
    private final int height;
    /** wallpaper_dim as an ARGB black, painted into each picture once instead of a full-screen shade view. */
    private final int dimColor;
    /** The picture on screen, released once the next one has been drawn. */
    private Bitmap current;
    private boolean active;
    private boolean closed;
    private boolean loading;
    private String displayed = "";
    /** wallpaper_captions: the shown picture's name from wallpapers/captions.txt; null when off or there are none. */
    private final TextView caption;
    private final Map<String, String> names;
    /** wallpaper_moods: the collection's groups by time of day; empty rotates through all of it. */
    private final Map<String, Set<String>> moods;
    /** config.xml latitude and longitude for the sun's times, and today's {sunrise, sunset} once worked out. */
    private final String latitude, longitude;
    private LocalDate sunDay;
    private int[] sun;

    WallpaperPlayer(Context context, FrameLayout root, Config config) {
        this.root = root;
        backgroundColor = config.backgroundColor;
        files = new ArrayList<>(config.wallpapers);
        interval = config.wallpaperRotationMinutes * 60_000L;
        bitmapConfig = config.wallpaperTrueColor ? Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888 : Bitmap.Config.RGB_565;
        // The dim is painted into the picture (decode), so no full-screen shade layer is drawn on every frame.
        dimColor = config.wallpaperDim > 0 ? (config.wallpaperDim * 255 / 100) << 24 : 0;
        order = config.wallpaperOrder;
        preferences = context.getSharedPreferences("wallpaper_rotation", Context.MODE_PRIVATE);
        moods = config.wallpaperMoods;
        latitude = moods.isEmpty() ? "" : context.getString(R.string.latitude);
        longitude = moods.isEmpty() ? "" : context.getString(R.string.longitude);
        // Playback state belongs to one collection. Changing the collection starts from its first
        // picture instead of resuming a filename that belonged to the previous one.
        String collection = collectionKey(files);
        if (!collection.equals(preferences.getString("collection", ""))) {
            preferences.edit().putString("collection", collection)
                    .remove("image").remove("changed").apply();
        }
        DisplayMetrics metrics = context.getResources().getDisplayMetrics();
        width = metrics.widthPixels;
        height = metrics.heightPixels;
        image = new ImageView(context);
        image.setScaleType(ImageView.ScaleType.CENTER_CROP);
        image.setImportantForAccessibility(View.IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_NO);
        names = config.wallpaperCaptions && config.wallpaperEnabled && !files.isEmpty()
                ? WallpaperCaptions.read(files.get(0).getParentFile()) : Collections.emptyMap();
        caption = names.isEmpty() ? null : makeCaption(context, root);
        if (config.wallpaperEnabled && !files.isEmpty()) {
            root.addView(image, 0, new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
                    ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT, ViewGroup.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT));
            showFirst();
        }
    }

    /**
     * The picture Home opens with is decoded right here, on the main thread, as the single wallpaper always was:
     * Home's first frame already has it instead of drawing the plain colour and the picture popping in later.
     * Only the later changes of a rotation decode in the background.
     */
    private void showFirst() {
        String previous = preferences.getString("image", "");
        List<File> playable = playable();
        File first = WallpaperRotation.find(playable, previous);
        if (first == null) first = WallpaperRotation.pick(playable, previous, order, random);
        while (first != null) {
            Bitmap bitmap = decode(first);
            if (bitmap != null) {
                show(bitmap);
                // The picture covers the whole screen: the root's plain colour under it is overdraw.
                root.setBackground(null);
                displayed = first.getName();
                showCaption(false);
                if (!displayed.equals(previous)) {
                    preferences.edit().putString("image", displayed)
                            .putLong("changed", System.currentTimeMillis()).apply();
                }
                return;
            }
            files.remove(first);   // unreadable or over 4K: try another, or keep the plain colour
            playable = playable();
            first = WallpaperRotation.pick(playable, previous, order, random);
        }
    }

    void start() {
        active = true;
        update();
    }

    void stop() {
        active = false;
    }

    /** Drops the wallpaper texture when Home is hidden and Android asks the process to free memory. */
    void releaseForMemoryPressure() {
        if (current == null) return;
        image.setImageDrawable(null);
        // The renderer may still have a queued frame that references this hardware bitmap. Drop our references and
        // let Android reclaim its native buffer after rendering releases it instead of recycling it mid-frame.
        current = null;
        displayed = "";
        root.setBackgroundColor(backgroundColor);
    }

    /** The pictures the rotation picks from now: wallpaper_moods' group for the time of day, or the whole collection. */
    private List<File> playable() {
        if (moods.isEmpty()) return files;
        LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now();
        if (!now.toLocalDate().equals(sunDay)) {
            sunDay = now.toLocalDate();
            sun = WallpaperMood.sun(sunDay, latitude, longitude, ZoneId.systemDefault());
        }
        return WallpaperMood.select(files, moods, WallpaperMood.timeOfDay(now.getHour() * 60 + now.getMinute(), sun[0], sun[1]));
    }

    void close() {
        active = false;
        closed = true;
        decoder.shutdownNow();
    }

    void update() {
        if (!active || closed || loading || files.isEmpty()) return;
        String previous = preferences.getString("image", "");
        // A picture outside the time of day's group (the group changed) is replaced at once, not after the interval.
        List<File> playable = playable();
        File selected = WallpaperRotation.find(playable, previous);
        long changed = preferences.getLong("changed", 0);
        if (selected == null || WallpaperRotation.due(changed, System.currentTimeMillis(), interval)) {
            selected = WallpaperRotation.pick(playable, previous, order, random);
        }
        if (selected == null || selected.getName().equals(displayed)) return;
        File next = selected;
        loading = true;
        decoder.execute(() -> {
            Bitmap bitmap = decode(next);
            root.post(() -> {
                loading = false;
                if (closed || !active) {
                    if (bitmap != null) bitmap.recycle();
                    return;
                }
                if (bitmap == null) {
                    files.remove(next);
                    Log.w("TvHome.Wallpaper", "Skipping unreadable image: " + next.getName());
                    update();
                    return;
                }
                show(bitmap);
                displayed = next.getName();
                showCaption(true);
                if (!displayed.equals(previous) || changed == 0) {
                    preferences.edit().putString("image", displayed)
                            .putLong("changed", System.currentTimeMillis()).apply();
                }
            });
        });
    }

    /**
     * Small light text under the top-right buttons, above everything else and never focusable. It sits where the
     * top bar ends in every layout, so it does not cover the clock, the stats line or the tiles.
     */
    private static TextView makeCaption(Context context, FrameLayout root) {
        float dp = context.getResources().getDisplayMetrics().density;
        TextView text = new TextView(context);
        text.setTextSize(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_SP, 15);
        text.setTextColor(0xD9FFFFFF);
        text.setShadowLayer(6 * dp, 0, dp, 0xCC000000);
        text.setSingleLine(true);
        text.setEllipsize(TextUtils.TruncateAt.END);
        text.setMaxWidth(Math.round(520 * dp));
        text.setFocusable(false);
        text.setAlpha(0f);
        try {
            text.setTypeface(UiFont.get(context, R.string.font_regular));
        } catch (Exception ignored) {
            // the system font is fine
        }
        FrameLayout.LayoutParams params = new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT,
                ViewGroup.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT, Gravity.TOP | Gravity.END);
        params.topMargin = Math.round(110 * dp);
        params.setMarginEnd(Math.round(62 * dp));
        root.addView(text, params);
        return text;
    }

    /** The displayed picture's name, faded across a change; a picture without a name hides the caption. */
    private void showCaption(boolean fade) {
        if (caption == null) return;
        String name = names.get(displayed);
        caption.animate().cancel();
        if (name == null) {
            caption.setAlpha(0f);
            return;
        }
        caption.setContentDescription(name);
        if (!fade || caption.getAlpha() == 0f) {
            caption.setText(name);
            caption.setAlpha(1f);
            return;
        }
        caption.animate().alpha(0f).setDuration(250).withEndAction(() -> {
            caption.setText(name);
            caption.animate().alpha(1f).setDuration(350).start();
        }).start();
    }

    /** Names plus sizes: enough to notice a different collection without hashing every image. */
    private static String collectionKey(List<File> images) {
        StringBuilder key = new StringBuilder();
        for (File file : images) key.append(file.getName()).append(':').append(file.length()).append(';');
        return key.toString();
    }

    /** Puts a picture on screen and releases the previous one after a frame has drawn the new one. */
    private void show(Bitmap bitmap) {
        Bitmap old = current;
        current = bitmap;
        // The wallpaper covers the whole root; avoid drawing the fallback colour under it.
        root.setBackground(null);
        image.setImageBitmap(bitmap);
        if (old != null && old != bitmap) image.postDelayed(old::recycle, 500);
    }

    private Bitmap decode(File file) {
        try {
            BitmapFactory.Options options = new BitmapFactory.Options();
            options.inJustDecodeBounds = true;
            BitmapFactory.decodeFile(file.getPath(), options);
            int width = options.outWidth, height = options.outHeight;
            if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) return null;
            int sample = WallpaperSize.sampleSize(width, height, this.width, this.height);
            if (!WallpaperSize.accepted(width / sample, height / sample)) return null;
            options.inJustDecodeBounds = false;
            options.inSampleSize = sample;
            int[] scale = WallpaperSize.coverScale(width / sample, height / sample, this.width, this.height);
            if (scale != null) {
                options.inScaled = true;
                options.inDensity = scale[0];
                options.inTargetDensity = scale[1];
            }
            options.inPreferredConfig = bitmapConfig;
            options.inMutable = dimColor != 0;
            Bitmap decoded = BitmapFactory.decodeFile(file.getPath(), options);
            if (decoded == null) return null;
            if (dimColor != 0) new Canvas(decoded).drawColor(dimColor);
            // One copy in GPU memory instead of a software bitmap plus its texture; the decode stays off the UI
            // thread for rotations, and Home's return no longer uploads 4-8 MB to the GPU.
            Bitmap gpu = decoded.copy(Bitmap.Config.HARDWARE, false);
            if (gpu == null) return decoded;
            decoded.recycle();
            return gpu;
        } catch (Exception | OutOfMemoryError failure) {
            return null;
        }
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\WallpaperRotation.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

import java.io.File;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Random;

final class WallpaperRotation {
    /** Playback orders persisted in config.json (wallpaper_order). */
    static final String ORDER_SEQUENTIAL = "sequential";
    static final String ORDER_SHUFFLE = "shuffle";

    static boolean validOrder(String order) {
        return ORDER_SEQUENTIAL.equals(order) || ORDER_SHUFFLE.equals(order);
    }

    static List<File> images(File directory) {
        List<File> result = new ArrayList<>();
        File[] entries = directory == null ? null : directory.listFiles();
        if (entries == null) return result;
        Arrays.sort(entries, Comparator.comparing(File::getName));
        for (File entry : entries) {
            String name = entry.getName().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
            if (entry.isFile() && entry.length() > 0 && entry.length() <= 10 * 1024 * 1024
                    && (name.endsWith(".jpg") || name.endsWith(".jpeg")
                    || name.endsWith(".png") || name.endsWith(".webp"))) {
                result.add(entry);
                if (result.size() == 100) break;
            }
        }
        return result;
    }

    static File find(List<File> images, String name) {
        for (File image : images) if (image.getName().equals(name)) return image;
        return null;
    }

    /** The on-TV choice (Launcher settings, Wallpaper) that turns the wallpaper off. */
    static final String CHOICE_NONE = "none";

    /**
     * What an on-TV wallpaper choice puts on Home in place of the theme's rotation: null when the theme decides
     * (no choice, or a picture that is no longer there), an empty list for {@link #CHOICE_NONE}, or the one picture
     * chosen from the theme's collection or its single {@code single} wallpaper.
     */
    static List<File> chosen(List<File> collection, File single, String choice) {
        if (choice == null) return null;
        if (CHOICE_NONE.equals(choice)) return Collections.emptyList();
        File picked = find(collection, choice);
        if (picked == null && single != null && choice.equals(single.getName())) picked = single;
        return picked == null ? null : Collections.singletonList(picked);
    }

    static File pick(List<File> images, String previous, Random random) {
        List<File> candidates = new ArrayList<>(images);
        if (candidates.size() > 1) candidates.removeIf(image -> image.getName().equals(previous));
        return candidates.isEmpty() ? null : candidates.get(random.nextInt(candidates.size()));
    }

    /**
     * The next picture in the sorted collection, wrapping to the first at the end. The list from
     * {@link #images(File)} is sorted by filename, so this is a stable order across restarts. A
     * previous name that is no longer in the collection starts again at the first picture.
     */
    static File next(List<File> images, String previous) {
        if (images.isEmpty()) return null;
        for (int i = 0; i < images.size(); i++) {
            if (images.get(i).getName().equals(previous)) {
                return images.get((i + 1) % images.size());
            }
        }
        return images.get(0);
    }

    /** Picks the next picture for {@code order}; an unknown order keeps the historical shuffle. */
    static File pick(List<File> images, String previous, String order, Random random) {
        return ORDER_SEQUENTIAL.equals(order) ? next(images, previous) : pick(images, previous, random);
    }

    static boolean due(long previous, long now, long interval) {
        // The minute tick is a Handler postDelayed, so it drifts by tens of milliseconds and often lands a few
        // hundred short of the interval. Compared exactly, that pass is skipped and the picture waits a whole
        // extra interval - a one-minute collection then changes every two. Two seconds of slack absorbs the
        // drift without letting a genuinely early call advance the picture.
        long slack = Math.min(2_000L, interval / 10);
        return interval > 0 && (previous == 0 || now < previous || now - previous >= interval - slack);
    }
}
`n`n========== FILE: launcher\app\src\main\java\com\gathin\tvhome\WallpaperSize.java ==========
package com.gathin.tvhome;

/**
 * How big a theme's wallpaper may be and what size it is decoded at (#166). A 1 GB TV cannot afford a
 * picture decoded at full size: a 65535x2159 image is about 283 MB even in RGB_565.
 */
final class WallpaperSize {
    private WallpaperSize() { }

    /** 4K UHD (3840x2160, 8.3 M pixels) and a little more; anything bigger is refused. */
    static final long MAX_PIXELS = 8_400_000L;

    static boolean accepted(int width, int height) {
        return width > 0 && height > 0 && (long) width * height <= MAX_PIXELS;
    }

    /** The largest power-of-two sample size that still covers the screen in both directions. */
    static int sampleSize(int width, int height, int screenW, int screenH) {
        int sample = 1;
        while (width / (sample * 2) >= screenW && height / (sample * 2) >= screenH) sample *= 2;
        return sample;
    }

    /**
     * {inDensity, inTargetDensity} that scale a (sampled) picture down to what CENTER_CROP shows: the
     * side that limits the cover lands on the screen size. Null when it is already that small.
     */
    static int[] coverScale(int width, int height, int screenW, int screenH) {
        if ((long) screenW * height >= (long) screenH * width) {   // width limits the cover
            return width > screenW ? new int[]{width, screenW} : null;
        }
        return height > screenH ? new int[]{height, screenH} : null;
    }
}

    <!-- Whether HomeKeyService and InputKeyService actually request key filtering (config.xml or a theme's

    <bool name="key_filter">true</bool>

    <!-- With key_filter on, true makes HomeKeyService and InputKeyService stop filtering keys while a game

    <bool name="gamepad_passthrough">false</bool>

    <bool name="consume_volume_keys">false</bool>

    <!-- With key_filter on, a volume change stops HomeKeyService and InputKeyService filtering keys for 4 s. For

    <bool name="volume_pauses_filter">false</bool>

    <integer-array name="settings_key_scancodes">

    <bool name="settings_key_panel">false</bool>

    <!-- Remote buttons that open an app, as "keycode:package" or "KEYCODE_NAME:package" (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 or
         HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1; both read this one list, and a theme's config.json can set it too). On Google TV the
         YouTube button sends 190 (KEYCODE_BUTTON_3) to the stock launcher, so it does nothing once launcherx
         is disabled (Chromecast with Google TV, Xiaomi MiTV-AXFR2): 190:com.google.android.youtube.tv brings
         it back. The KTC LUMIO VISION remote (Realtek Google TV) sends Netflix 191, YouTube 190, Prime Video 195
         and TL;DR 200. Some remotes send several app buttons as one keycode and tell them apart only by scancode
         (Sony BRAVIA: YouTube, Prime Video and Disney+ are all keycode 196, scancodes 485, 490 and 491); list those
         as "scan:scancode:package", e.g. scan:490:com.wbd.hbomax, found with `tools/tv.py 'getevent -t'` (the
         EV_KEY code: the hex number after 0001 on the button's line, written in decimal, so 01ea is 490). A
         scancode entry wins over a keycode. In place of a package, "input:<input id>"
         switches to that TV input, e.g. scan:227:input:com.tcl.tvinput/.passthroughinput.TvPassThroughService/HW1413744640
         for HDMI 3 on a TCL Smart TV Pro; the ids are in `tools/tv.py 'dumpsys tv_input'` (hdmi_port=N under
         TvInputHardwareInfo). An action word in place of a package runs that action instead: back, home, recents,
         mute (toggles the sound, with the TV's volume bar), sleep (standby, Android 9 and later), screensaver (the
         one chosen in the TV's settings, or the launcher's clock), settings, wifi, library (Home with the App
         library open; with app_library off it only brings Home forward, so a remote's Apps button, which sends
         284 KEYCODE_ALL_APPS, can open it: 284:library) or ignore (swallows the button: it
         does nothing, for a shortcut pressed by accident; find its scancode with `tools/tv.py 'getevent -t'`);
         e.g. KEYCODE_PROG_YELLOW:mute, scan:586:ignore and hold:KEYCODE_PROG_YELLOW:sleep. "package/.Activity" opens that activity instead of the app's launcher
         entry, e.g. hold:191:io.github.maxhayim.brightness/.QuickActivity for an add-on's quick bar. Prefix an
         entry with "hold:" for the same button's long press:
         "hold:KEYCODE_BUTTON_8:org.xbmc.kodi" opens Kodi when held for half a second, while the unprefixed entry
         still opens on a tap; "hold:scan:490:..." works for scancodes. A key with only a hold entry does nothing
         on a tap. A listed app that is not installed leaves the button doing nothing. Prefix an entry with "front:"
         for what a tap does while the button's own app is already in front (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1), and use
         "guide:<package>" as a target to open that Live TV app's program guide: "172:com.vt.tv.tvcenter" with
         "front:172:guide:com.vt.tv.tvcenter" makes the Hisense hengshan Live TV button open Live TV, then its guide,
         where the firmware hands KEYCODE_GUIDE (172) to the stock launcher and no app ever receives it. Leave empty
         to omit. -->
    <string-array name="app_keys" translatable="false">

    <!-- The Inputs list shows only HDMI ports and CEC devices that report connected. Empty ports, devices asleep in

         sleeping device has) and the AV jacks fold behind a "More inputs" row that expands the rest. An HDMI row
         whose state the TV cannot be trusted with stays. Off by default: every input is listed. Can also be set
         with "inputs_connected_only" in a theme. -->
    <bool name="inputs_connected_only">false</bool>
    <!-- Only CEC device rows in the Inputs list show a connection state ("Steam Deck · HDMI 1  Connected"); bare HDMI
         ports show none. For TVs whose port states land on the wrong port: TCL UnionTV (Android 9) reports the empty
         HDMI 1 as connected and a device on HDMI 2 nowhere, while its CEC device list stays right. A device without
         CEC then shows no state at all. Off by default. Can also be set with "inputs_cec_state_only" in a theme. -->
    <bool name="inputs_cec_state_only">false</bool>
    <!-- Names under every tile, not only the focused one: unfocused names stay dimmed, the focused one is full white.
         With dock_row the band grows down to hold the dock's names too. -->
    <bool name="always_show_names">false</bool>
    <!-- Wallpapers decode as RGB_565 (2 bytes a pixel, 4 MB at 1080p), which bands dark gradients such as a night
         sky, most of all under wallpaper_dim. true decodes them in 32-bit colour: 8 MB, for TVs with 2 GB or more. -->
    <bool name="wallpaper_true_color">false</bool>
    <!-- Rotating wallpapers: show each picture's name under the top-right buttons, from a captions.txt next to the
         pictures in wallpapers/ ("01-dusk.jpg<TAB>Dusk over the peaks", one per line). A picture without a line
         shows no name. Can also be set with "wallpaper_captions": true in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="wallpaper_captions">false</bool>
    <!-- Rotating wallpapers grouped by the time of day, as JSON: {"morning": [file names], "evening": [...],
         "night": [...]}. While set, the rotation picks only from the group that fits now: morning from sunrise to
         noon, evening until half an hour after sunset, night the rest, with the sun at latitude and longitude (07:00
         and 18:30 without them). It moves to the new group as soon as the time of day changes. A missing or empty
         group falls back to the whole collection; empty rotates through every picture. A theme can set
         "wallpaper_moods" as an object. -->
    <string name="wallpaper_moods" translatable="false"></string>
    <!-- Hold OK on a tile opens a small menu: Move (picks the tile up for reordering), Remove from Home (only with
         app_library) and App info. On by default since 3.3; false keeps the old behaviour: holding OK opens the app's
         App info page. A theme's config.json can set "tile_menu" either way. -->
    <bool name="tile_menu">true</bool>

    <!-- Grid rows left visible under the dock on the home screen. 0 = dock sits at the very bottom. Tiles shrink if
         the dock, its title and this many rows would not otherwise fit the screen height. -->
    <integer name="rows_below_dock">0</integer>

    <!-- The focused dock app's name in large type above the dock. false keeps only the glow, which leaves room
         for bigger tiles when rows_below_dock is 2 or 3. -->
    <bool name="dock_title">true</bool>

    <!-- Tiles per row in the grid; the dock always has this many slots. Tiles are 180dp wide at 4 columns and
         shrink to fit from 5 up (about 144dp at 5, 117dp at 6 on a 1080p TV). -->
    <integer name="columns">4</integer>

    <!-- Basic motion is on; advanced effects are opt-in in the launcher's own Settings screen. -->
    <bool name="animations">true</bool>
    <bool name="advanced_effects">false</bool>

    <!-- Optional Default-home tile; keep this key for existing themes and tile-ordering work.
         Off by default because the chooser is also available from launcher settings. -->
    <bool name="show_home_settings_shortcut">false</bool>

    <!-- Installed launchable apps, including ordinary Android apps. Also settable in config.json. -->
    <bool name="app_library">false</bool>
    <!-- Every app tile is its icon on a card tinted from that icon, name only under the focused tile,
         instead of each app's own banner. Off by default; a theme can set "uniform_tiles": true. -->
    <bool name="uniform_tiles">false</bool>
    <!-- Optional direct Home picker in the app library: OK toggles the checkmark, checked apps first.
         Off by default; a theme can set "app_library_selection": true (also needs app_library). -->
    <bool name="app_library_selection">false</bool>
    <!-- OK opens every app in the library, not only the apps on Home: for a library that holds the apps a theme
         keeps off Home with hidden_apps. Hold OK still offers Add to Home. app_library_selection wins when both are
         on. Off by default; a theme can set "library_ok_opens": true (also needs app_library). -->
    <bool name="library_ok_opens">false</bool>

    <!-- Apps pre-seeded into the App library's "added" set at startup (config.xml library_apps, or a theme's
         config.json). They show on Home as if the owner had added them in the App library UI, and stay
         removable there (a removed one stays hidden). For sets where almost no app declares a leanback entry
         (many China-market TVs, e.g. Coocaa 8R145), a fresh Home with app_library on would otherwise be
         nearly empty. Empty (off) by default, so existing setups change nothing. -->
    <string-array name="library_apps" translatable="false">
    </string-array>

    <!-- Packages the App library catalogue never offers, even with app_library on (config.xml
         library_excluded_apps, or a theme's config.json). Different from hidden_apps, which only keeps a
         package off Home while still listing it here: some boards hide a package because opening it is
         unsafe (a factory-test menu that can misconfigure the TV), and the catalogue otherwise ignores
         hidden_apps and offers it as "Add to Home" anyway. Empty (off) by default, so existing setups
         change nothing. -->
    <string-array name="library_excluded_apps" translatable="false">
    </string-array>

    <!-- Module cards: an app that declares a card (docs/specs/card.md) can stand in for its tile with its own
         label, caption and glow colour, once you answer Show on the prompt. false: never look for cards or ask. -->
    <bool name="module_cards">true</bool>

    <!-- Reduced motion: for TVs whose GPU cannot keep up (MediaTek MT5895 on Android 10 is the known case).
         true keeps the GPU drawing path but calms the movement and draws far fewer frames: the highlight
         slides with no bounce and settles within 5 frames, every animation lasts 90 ms or less, names, top
         shelf, glow and highlight appear instead of fading, and there is no tile entrance. Set it
         here or with "reduced_motion": true in a theme's config.json; false keeps the normal motion. -->
    <bool name="reduced_motion">false</bool>

    <!-- The glass highlight springs past the tile it moves to and the focused tile zooms past its size
         before settling. false: both go straight there, with no bounce, while scrolling stays smooth
         (reduced_motion also removes the overshoot, but scrolls in one jump). Can also be set with
         "focus_overshoot" in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="focus_overshoot">true</bool>

    <!-- One line under the clock: CPU, free memory and free storage. Off by default; a theme can set
         "show_stats": true. Nothing is read, and the clock does not move, while this is false. -->
    <bool name="show_stats">false</bool>

    <!-- Each team's next game in the F1 panel's place under the clock, rotating with the theme's F1 weekend: the package
         of an add-on that publishes them (the Game Day add-on: io.github.justinnewman.gameday; contract in docs/modules.md).
         Empty = off: nothing is read or watched. The launcher only reads what the add-on publishes and never goes
         online. A theme can set "game_day". -->
    <string name="game_day" translatable="false"></string>

    <!-- Time-of-day backdrop behind everything: a dark gradient that follows the clock, with a warm
         horizon glow around sunrise and sunset. 0 keeps the plain background (the default); 1 to 100
         sets its opacity. Around 60 reads clearly without hiding a wallpaper. Can also be set with
         "sky_intensity": 60 in a theme's config.json. -->
    <integer name="sky_intensity">0</integer>
    <!-- Where the TV is, in decimal degrees, so the sky's sunrise and sunset glows follow the real sun
         (computed on the TV, no network). Empty: a fixed temperate day, sunset glow around 19:00.
         Vilnius: 54.69 and 25.28. -->
    <string name="latitude" translatable="false"></string>
    <string name="longitude" translatable="false"></string>

    <!-- Cinematic top shelf: the focused dock app's artwork, softened, fills the top of the screen in its
         colour; the shelf gets a larger name, a "Last opened" line (from the apps Home opened) and dock position
         dots, the focus glow takes the app's colour and the dock band turns translucent. false keeps the plain
         shelf. Can also be set with "cinematic_home": true in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="cinematic_home">false</bool>
    <!-- With cinematic_home, false leaves out the dock position dots under the app's name, for a quieter shelf. Can
         also be set with "cinematic_dots": false in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="cinematic_dots">true</bool>
    <!-- With cinematic_home, true keeps the focus highlight white on the dock instead of the focused app's colour,
         for wallpapers and banners that clash with it; app_glow still colours every tile. Can also be set with
         "cinematic_white_focus": true in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="cinematic_white_focus">false</bool>
    <!-- With cinematic_home, how much of a wallpaper the shelf covers: cinematic_scrim is the strength of the dark
         scrim that keeps the name readable (0 to 100 percent, 100 as before) and cinematic_art the opacity of the
         app's softened artwork (0 to 100, 50 as before; 0 leaves the wallpaper uncovered). Lower values let a
         theme's wallpaper show through. A theme can set "cinematic_scrim" and "cinematic_art". -->
    <integer name="cinematic_scrim">45</integer>
    <integer name="cinematic_art">75</integer>

    <!-- The glow behind the dock in the focused app's colour (red for YouTube, blue for Prime Video). false keeps
         only background_color or the wallpaper behind everything. Can also be set with "ambient_glow": false in a
         theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="ambient_glow">true</bool>
    <!-- true: when the focus moves to an app of another colour, the ambient glow takes the new colour in one frame
         instead of dimming and fading back in. Each frame of that fade repaints the whole screen, about 40 per key
         press, which a slow GPU such as the Mali-G52 cannot keep up with. Can also be set with "glow_snap" in a
         theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="glow_snap">false</bool>
    <!-- The focus highlight glows in the focused app's colour on every tile, as the cinematic shelf does for the
         dock, without cinematic_home. Can also be set with "app_glow": true in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="app_glow">false</bool>
    <!-- The rows fade out as they scroll up under the clock, instead of being cut off at a hard line (TopFade).
         The grid then draws into a hardware layer, about 6 MB of graphics memory at 1080p, so it is off by default.
         Can also be set with "fade_rows": true in a theme's config.json. -->
    <bool name="fade_rows">false</bool>
    <!-- Minutes Home may sit untouched before it shows the clock screensaver (ClockActivity); 0 turns it off.
         Unlike the system screensaver this never starts over live TV or an app, which matters on TVs whose
         Live TV window does not keep the screen on (CVTE): there the system screensaver would start in the
         middle of a programme. Can also be set with "home_idle_clock_minutes": 10 in a theme's config.json. -->
    <integer name="home_idle_clock_minutes">10</integer>
    <!-- Back on the Home screen opens the clock screensaver (ClockActivity, the same screen as
         home_idle_clock_minutes). Back keeps working as usual inside apps and Settings; only Home's own Back
         press changes. Off by default (Back does nothing on Home); a theme can set "back_opens_clock": true. -->
    <bool name="back_opens_clock">false</bool>
    <!-- The clock screensaver (Home idle clock and the system screensaver) over Home's wallpaper instead of black with
         a coloured glow. The clock still moves every minute. Can also be set with "clock_wallpaper" in a theme. -->
    <bool name="clock_wallpaper">true</bool>
    <!-- How dark that wallpaper is behind the clock, 0 to 90 %. Can also be set with "clock_wallpaper_dim". -->
    <integer name="clock_wallpaper_dim">50</integer>
    <!-- The clock screensaver's slow coloured glow behind the clock. false leaves the clock and date alone on plain black
         (OLED panels); they still move every minute. Ignored while clock_wallpaper shows a picture. Can also be set
         with "clock_glow" in a theme. -->
    <bool name="clock_glow">true</bool>
    <!-- Shape of the glow behind the focused app, in its colour: radial (a soft glow, the default) or horizon (the
         colour washes down from the top edge and fades to black, brightest along the top). The cinematic shelf
         keeps its own glow. Can also be set with "glow_style": "horizon" in a theme's config.json. -->
    <string name="glow_style" translatable="false">radial</string>
    <!-- The focus highlight's look: glass (the default: a translucent slab with a bright top sheen, a crisp rim and a
         faint outer glow), rim (the crisp rim alone, no sheen, fill or glow, for a quiet focus over a wallpaper) or
         halo (the rim with a lighter outer glow). Can also be set with "glass_style": "rim" in a theme's config.json. -->
    <string name="glass_style" translatable="false">glass</string>

    <!-- Tiles drawn from the app's icon and name instead of its banner (for banners that crop badly). -->
    <string-array name="icon_tiles" translatable="false">
    </string-array>
</resources>

<!-- Keys only: no accessibilityEventTypes (0), so the system never calls into the launcher for
     accessibility events, which both services ignore. Key filtering depends only on
     flagRequestFilterKeyEvents and canRequestFilterKeyEvents, not on the event types.
     stock_home_redirect is the exception: with it set, HomeKeyService adds typeWindowStateChanged at runtime. -->
<accessibility-service xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    android:accessibilityFeedbackType="feedbackGeneric"
    android:accessibilityFlags="flagRequestFilterKeyEvents"
    android:canRequestFilterKeyEvents="true"
    android:description="@string/home_key_description" />
